body:
## How long does an office fitout in Newcastle take?

There is no dependable completion period without the actual premises, scope, design, approval pathway, procurement and access arrangements. A contractor's time on site is only part of the programme. Decisions made before work starts can determine whether that site date is achievable.

This guide shows how to build a decision-based programme for a Newcastle office project. It is a planning method, not a standard duration or a promise of completion. YOS acts as your [client-side FitOut project manager](/office-fitout); the appointed builder, consultants, suppliers and relevant authorities retain their own responsibilities.

**Use the working register:** [Download the FitOut programme and decisions worksheet (TXT)](/guides/office-fitout-programme-newcastle.txt). It has fields for dependencies, evidence, decision owners and revised dates. No email is required.

## Separate four dates that are often confused

Before discussing a number of weeks, establish what the date refers to.

| Milestone | What must be clarified |
| --- | --- |
| Premises available | When access is actually available, with landlord or existing-tenant dependencies |
| Construction start | What design, appointments, approvals and site conditions must be resolved first |
| Construction completion | The applicable contractual milestone and evidence required from the appointed team |
| Business ready to operate | Required occupation conditions, IT, furniture, staff access and operating arrangements |

Do not treat those dates as interchangeable. A signed lease does not establish construction readiness, and a visually finished room does not show that the business can operate from it.

## Build the sequence before fixing the calendar

Map the workstreams and ask the responsible people what must precede each one. Some can proceed in parallel; others cannot. Use the actual project team's advice rather than assuming this example sequence applies unchanged.

1. Approve the business brief and essentials for opening.
2. Investigate the premises and confirm landlord and existing-condition inputs.
3. Test the layout, services requirements and preliminary whole-project budget.
4. Coordinate design, approval responsibilities and procurement documentation.
5. Confirm the required permissions, appointments, site access and ordering decisions.
6. Carry out the appointed contractors' work and coordinate deliveries.
7. Complete the required inspections, testing, documentation and outstanding actions.
8. Check operational readiness before the move and first working day.

For the wider brief and approval questions, use our [Newcastle office fitout planning checklist](/blog/office-fitout-newcastle-planning-checklist). The programme should reference the same scope revision as the budget and proposals.

## Ask who owns each prerequisite

A date without an owner and evidence can become an assumption that nobody notices. Give each critical input a named responsible role and record what confirms it is complete.

| Input | Owner to nominate | Evidence to request |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Business brief | Client decision maker | Approved scope and priorities |
| Landlord input | Agreed landlord or managing-agent contact | Required information and written decisions |
| Approval pathway | Appointed planning adviser or certifier, as applicable | Project-specific pathway, prerequisites and responsibilities |
| Design package | Appointed designers and consultants | Coordinated revision suitable for its intended use |
| Supplier order | Authorised client and supplier contacts | Exact specification, approval status and confirmed timing basis |
| Site readiness | Appointed contractor and relevant site contacts | Required conditions, access and work sequence confirmed |
| Operating readiness | Client IT, operations and project team | Agreed tests, documentation and unresolved actions |

The NSW Planning Portal describes different planning approval pathways. It does not establish which pathway applies to your tenancy or give your project a guaranteed determination date. Have the appointed advisers assess the actual works, use and site; keep landlord consent and statutory requirements distinct.

## Identify the decisions that can stop procurement

Ask suppliers when the timing starts: accepted order, payment, approved drawings, finish selection or another event. Record manufacturing, dispatch, delivery and installation separately where they are different milestones.

For made-to-order joinery or furniture, an unresolved drawing or finish can leave the order unreleased even when a budget has been approved. Ask what information is needed and who can approve substitutions. Do not assume a shorter advertised product lead time applies to the exact quantity, finish and destination.

Connect the programme with the [furniture installation scope](/blog/office-furniture-installation-checklist-newcastle) and [standard, modified or custom furniture decision](/blog/standard-modified-custom-office-furniture-newcastle). Keep quoted lead times dated and distinguish an estimate from a confirmed commitment.

## Illustrative example: a late decision changes the sequence

Imagine a fictional project where a supplier requires approved drawings before starting a five-week manufacturing period. The order was planned for release at the end of week three, with delivery at the end of week eight. Drawing approval instead arrives at the end of week five.

If the manufacturing duration and every other assumption stay unchanged, delivery moves to the end of week ten. That is two weeks later for this one workstream. It is not proof that the entire project must move by two weeks: the project team must assess dependencies, available float, alternatives and the effect on opening-day requirements.

These weeks are invented to explain dependency arithmetic. They are not Newcastle supplier benchmarks, YOS delivery commitments or a recommended construction programme.

Useful responses include resolving the decision earlier, asking about a suitable alternative, adjusting staging or revising the operating date. An earlier date should not be recovered by silently omitting required checks or assuming an approval will arrive.

## Plan an occupied refurbishment as a separate option

If people must remain working, record occupied zones, staff and visitor routes, noisy or dusty work, shutdowns, deliveries, temporary meeting arrangements and IT changeovers with the appointed project team. They must assess safe arrangements and suitability for the actual work.

Compare staging with temporarily relocating or taking an area out of use. Each option can affect access, sequencing, repeated mobilisation and business operations. A staged project is not automatically faster or cheaper, and after-hours work is subject to actual availability and building rules.

A Newcastle CBD building may have goods-lift or loading restrictions, but those are site questions to confirm with building management, not universal local rules.

## Update the programme when the scope changes

Record the proposed change, reason, affected specification, cost and programme impact. Name who recommends it, who can authorise it and which appointments or orders need updating. A verbal decision in a site conversation should not become an unrecorded change to everyone else's brief.

Review the next decisions with the project team. Separate completed evidence from “expected soon”, and explain which target dates rely on unresolved inputs. When a date moves, update the affected dependencies and let the responsible people confirm the revised plan.

Use the [warm-shell, cold-shell and finish-level budget guide](/blog/commercial-fitout-cost-newcastle-2026) to keep scope and cost decisions connected. The [FitOut estimator](/resources/fitout-estimator) is indicative and does not calculate a construction programme.

## Work backwards from the first working day

Agree the tests that demonstrate business readiness: access works, essential systems are usable, furniture is installed, required documents are available and critical outstanding items have been resolved by the responsible people. Obtain the required occupation and safety confirmations from the relevant appointed professionals.

Plan time for those checks and for addressing failures. A removalist booking is not evidence that occupation is permitted or practical. Use the [Friday handover test](/blog/office-fitout-handover-checklist) to rehearse an ordinary working day before relying on the move date.

## Bring the programme into the first conversation

Tell YOS the suburb, whether the premises are secured, what needs changing, whether the office must remain operating and the date the business hopes to open. Include a floor plan and mark the inputs that are still unconfirmed.

We can coordinate the client-side brief, budget, consultants, procurement decisions and handover within an agreed management scope. Construction and trade work remain with appropriately appointed and licensed contractors.

[Discuss your Newcastle office fitout programme](/office-fitout#fitout-enquiry). If you have not committed to premises, connect the workplace plan with [tenant representation](/tenant-rep) or [commercial buying advice](/buyers-agency) before the property decision.
